_lisezmoi: Traduction anglaise des articles (sources/actualites.json). Seuls les textes se traduisent : date, catégorie, images et ordre restent ceux du fichier français.

Chaque article est repéré par son slug français. « slug » donne son adresse anglaise (news/<slug>.html), puis titre, extrait, contenu (paragraphes), « image.alt » (description de la photo à la une, si le français en a une) et « galerie » (une description par photo, dans l'ordre du fichier français).
« categories » donne le nom anglais de chaque catégorie, repérée par son slug.
Dans WordPress : chaque article anglais est la traduction liée de l'article français (Polylang), avec ses propres catégories traduites.

gaboil-nouvelle-gouvernance.titre: GAB’OIL: new governance to meet performance requirements
gaboil-nouvelle-gouvernance.extrait: The distribution subsidiary of the Gabon Oil Group is entering a new stage in its development. Between financial assessment, profitability requirements and the consolidation of its governance, Gab’Oil intends to lay the foundations of a more solid and sustainable business model.

image.alt: A man hands a document to a woman in front of the official portrait of the Head of State, with a third man looking on

contenu: Appointed Chairman of the Board of Directors of Gab’Oil S.A. on 18 September 2026, Yves-Fernand Manfoumbi officially took office on 26 October, at a handover ceremony with his predecessor, Martial Rufin Moussavou.

This transition comes at a decisive moment for the company, whose petroleum product distribution activities hold an important place in the Gabon Oil Group's value chain and in supplying the national market.
On taking office, the new Chairman of the Board announced an in-depth 60-day assessment mission covering Gab’Oil's financial situation, profitability and governance mechanisms.

This approach is intended to establish a precise diagnosis, identify room for improvement and define a costed recovery plan. The stated objective is to restore the company's profitability on a lasting basis, while reducing its dependence on financial support from the State.

What is at stake, however, goes beyond the accounts alone. It also concerns Gab’Oil's ability to consolidate its operating model, control its costs and pursue its distribution missions under economically sustainable conditions.
For employees, this new stage calls for a collective effort around shared priorities: rigour, responsibility, efficiency and quality of service.
The next sixty days will be those of the diagnosis. The decisions that follow will have to turn its conclusions into measurable results.

naufrage-prospector-5.titre: Gabon – Sinking of the Prospector 5: one life lost, four missing and a nation put to the test
naufrage-prospector-5.extrait: On Saturday 24 October 2026, at 8:37 pm, the Prospector 5 drilling rig, owned by Borr Drilling and deployed by BW Energy Gabon on the Dussafu Marin permit, off Mayumba, sank in the Atlantic Ocean during a preloading operation.

image.alt: A tilted jack-up drilling rig sinking at sea at dusk, surrounded by vessels

contenu: Of the 115 people on board, 110 were rescued. The latest toll reports one death, four people still missing and six injured receiving care.
Behind this painful toll are bereaved families, loved ones holding on to hope and an entire professional community deeply affected.

The day after the tragedy, the President of the Republic, Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, travelled to Port-Gentil to meet the survivors. He expressed the solidarity of the Nation and set three requirements: continue the search, establish responsibilities through a technical investigation, and guarantee the safety of the installations and the protection of the environment before any resumption of activities.
His words resonate particularly in an industry where risk is part of daily life:
“Oil will never be worth more than a Gabonese life.”

This tragedy is a reminder of a reality that production imperatives must never obscure: behind every helmet, every coverall and every workstation there is a human life, with its plans, its loved ones and the hope of returning home.

Industrial safety cannot be limited to posted procedures or performance indicators. It is built through prevention, rigorous inspections, quality equipment and the ability of each person to stop an operation when safety conditions are not met.
As the search continues, our thoughts are with the person who died, the four missing, their families and the rescue teams deployed.
May this ordeal strengthen, throughout Gabon's oil industry, a shared conviction: no resource extracted, no barrel produced justifies the sacrifice of a life.

african-energy-week-2026.titre: African Energy Week 2026: the GOC Group showcases its activities and development prospects in Cape Town
african-energy-week-2026.extrait: One group, complementary businesses and a shared determination: to create more value from Gabon's energy resources.

image.alt: The Gabon Oil Company stand at African Energy Week, beneath a hanging sign bearing the logos of the Group and its subsidiaries

contenu: From 12 to 16 October 2026, in Cape Town, South Africa, the Gabon Oil Company (GOC) Group took part in African Energy Week (AEW), an international event bringing together players in the African energy industry.

With a 64 m² institutional stand, set up jointly with its subsidiary Assala Energy, the Group presented its activities, facilities and projects, illustrating its progressive integration across the entire hydrocarbon value chain, from upstream to downstream.
The stand also fostered business meetings and discussions on prospects for technical and commercial cooperation.

Oil production, gas value creation, industrial services, storage and distribution: the diversity of the businesses represented reflects the evolution of a national company that has become an integrated oil group.
In Cape Town, GOC showed the ground it has covered and the future it intends to build, drawing on its subsidiaries, skills and assets to contribute more to the Gabonese economy.

caps-avenir-energetique-afrique-centrale.titre: CAPS: GOC at the heart of discussions on the energy future of Central Africa
caps-avenir-energetique-afrique-centrale.extrait: Linking resources, bringing economies closer together and giving African energy cooperation a new dimension.

image.alt: A delegation gathered in front of the sign of the African Petroleum Producers' Organization

contenu: This is the vision behind the Central Africa Pipeline System (CAPS), whose memoranda of understanding were signed on 29 September 2026 in Brazzaville, in the presence of a Gabon Oil Company (GOC) delegation led by its Deputy Managing Director, Hervé Bertrand NNANG ENGUE.
This project, estimated at 14 billion dollars, provides for a network of oil and gas pipelines linking the six CEMAC countries, with the Gabon–Congo corridor identified as the priority route.
For GOC, an integrated national oil group, this prospect opens avenues for reflection on adding value to its gas resources, notably at Mboumba, and on their possible access to regional markets.
After Dongying, in China, then Brazzaville, GOC continues to follow the discussions on this project, whose completion remains subject to technical studies, institutional decisions and financing.
Because the stakes are concrete: enabling Africa's energy resources to contribute more to supplying the continent's industries, businesses and people.
The next discussions are scheduled in Abidjan, from 18 to 22 November 2026, at SIREXE.

cabef-2026-performance-industrielle.titre: CABEF 2026: GOC explores new solutions to strengthen its industrial performance
cabef-2026-performance-industrielle.extrait: From 28 to 31 August 2026, Gabon Oil Company (GOC) took part in the Central Africa Business and Energy Forum (CABEF), held in Dongying, China, alongside the 18th Oil Trade Fair in the Yellow River Delta. A mission devoted to finding technological solutions, financing and industrial cooperation suited to the Group's operational needs.

image.alt: Participants listening around a meeting table, during the meetings in Dongying

contenu: Led by the Deputy Managing Director, Hervé Bertrand NNANG ENGUE, the delegation brought together representatives of the Operations, Technical, HSEI, Gas and Communication departments.

During a panel on expertise, technology and innovation, the Deputy Managing Director set out the company's expectations: “We want suitable solutions and adequate financing in order to implement these technologies.”

This approach guided the meetings with several Chinese manufacturers, notably Shengji Petroleum Equipment, Deshi Group, KERUI and WLHI. Discussions covered drilling equipment, pumping, cementing, production optimisation and secure fuel storage facilities.

The industrial visits also made it possible to examine solutions that could meet specific needs: replacing the Mboumba living quarters, tank management, treating deposits that affect production and capturing associated gas for energy use.
At regional level, the discussions on the Central African Pipeline System (CAPS) underlined the importance of political backing, risk management and mobilising financing.
The mission also fostered exchanges between the subsidiaries ASSALA Energy and PIZOLUB. PIZOLUB notably explored options for sourcing base oils and additives.
At the end of the meetings, several avenues for cooperation were identified. They will have to undergo technical, economic and regulatory assessments before any decision is taken.

For GOC, the challenge now is to turn the contacts made in Dongying into concrete, reliable solutions suited to the realities of its facilities. An approach that places technological mastery, operational performance and industrial cooperation at the service of its ambitions.

nomination-dg-gaboil.titre: GAB’OIL: Éric Alain Sounda takes the helm of GOC's distribution subsidiary
nomination-dg-gaboil.extrait: Mr Éric Alain Sounda has been appointed Managing Director of Gab’Oil.

image.alt: Three men posing among guests in a hall

galerie.alt: Éric Alain Sounda, Managing Director of Gab'Oil

contenu: Following the Council of Ministers of 22 May 2026, chaired by the Head of State, Brigadier General BRICE CLOTAIRE OLIGUI NGUEMA, Mr ÉRIC ALAIN SOUNDA was appointed Managing Director of GAB’OIL, the distribution and marketing subsidiary of GABON OIL COMPANY (GOC). He succeeds Ms RENÉE PATRICIA KU-KUMBE IVUGU, who had headed the company for sixteen months.

This appointment comes as the highest authorities seek to stabilise the governance of this strategic subsidiary, which has seen several changes of management in recent years. Gab’Oil also faces major financial and structural challenges, including the restoration of its accounts and the settlement of significant cross-debts with other State-owned companies such as the Société Gabonaise de Raffinage (SOGARA) and the Société d'Énergie et d'Eau du Gabon (SEEG).

A seasoned insider, ÉRIC ALAIN SOUNDA has held important positions within the company, having previously served as Sales Director before working as Head of the Sales Department. His in-depth knowledge of the field, of distribution logistics and of customer relations will be essential to meet the company's profitability and efficiency challenges.

The priorities set for the new Managing Director include streamlining operating costs, restructuring internal teams, strengthening management transparency and modernising the national network of service stations. This network, which currently has 13 active stations across the country, spearheads the energy sovereignty and price regulation policy pursued by the GOC GROUP.

The General Management of GOC extends its warmest congratulations to Mr ÉRIC ALAIN SOUNDA and assures him of its full support in implementing his roadmap for the recovery and sustainable growth of GAB’OIL.

deploiement-gaboil.titre: Gab'Oil expansion: a network serving citizens
deploiement-gaboil.extrait: The national brand continues to extend its footprint, ever closer to the people.

image.alt: Gab'Oil service station: grey and red canopy, fuel pumps and oil-change workshop

contenu: In December 2025, Gab’Oil, a strategic subsidiary of GOC, confirmed its role as a key player in national energy security by pursuing an ambitious modernisation of its network.
2025 was marked by the opening of new modern stations, the renovation of existing infrastructure and improved service for customers.
Beyond distribution, every Gab’Oil station carries a mission: to make energy accessible everywhere, including in remote areas.

modernisation-outils.titre: Modernising management tools and transforming the organisation
modernisation-outils.extrait: A wide-ranging internal modernisation programme to strengthen overall performance.

image.alt: A delegation visiting an office equipped with workstations

contenu: GOC has launched a wide-ranging internal modernisation programme to strengthen its overall performance. This transformation rests first and foremost on the digitalisation of processes, which automates many tasks, shortens operational lead times and improves data reliability.
The company is also optimising its technical data flows, a key issue for obtaining real-time information on oil and gas operations.
However, this internal transformation cannot succeed without upskilling the teams. GOC is therefore rolling out continuous training programmes.

pizolub-renaissance.titre: Pizolub: an industrial revival that adds value locally
pizolub-renaissance.extrait: Pizolub confirms its return among the country's strategic industrial players.

image.alt: Operator in a helmet next to a yellow drum of lubricant, on a machine at the Pizolub plant

contenu: Based in Port-Gentil, Pizolub confirmed in 2025 its return among the country's strategic industrial players, driven by a modernisation programme led by GOC.
After several years of slowdown, Pizolub is upgrading its production lines, which now meet international standards.
This revival is part of GOC's strategy to reduce dependence on imports, stimulate local value chains and strengthen Gabon's industrial base.

tullow-oil-gop.titre: Tullow Oil Gabon becomes Gabon Oil Participations
tullow-oil-gop.extrait: A national strategy to consolidate and modernise the oil portfolio.

image.alt: A man and a woman talking, seated at a desk

contenu: The discussions surrounding the interests of Tullow Oil Gabon, now integrated under the name Gabon Oil Participations (GOP), are part of a clearly stated national strategy to consolidate and modernise the oil portfolio.
This gradual integration also makes it possible to optimise the national portfolio by harmonising asset management under a single strategic direction.
Finally, this transaction contributes directly to strengthening Gabon's long-term energy resilience.

smp-maintenance.titre: SMP: securing maintenance and technical expertise
smp-maintenance.extrait: GOC lays the foundations of a 100% Gabonese subsidiary dedicated to oil technical services.

image.alt: Technician in orange coveralls and a visor helmet, with a Gabonese flag badge on the shoulder

contenu: The takeover of the Société de Maintenance Pétrolière (SMP) is a key lever in GOC's strategy to strengthen its industrial base. By bringing this entity into its scope, GOC is laying the foundations of a 100% Gabonese subsidiary entirely dedicated to oil technical services.
This development marks a major turning point for the country's operational sovereignty. With SMP, GOC is able to consolidate cutting-edge local skills.
By bringing this expertise in-house, GOC improves cost control, raises the quality of its interventions and ensures greater responsiveness at production sites.

assala-energy.extrait: The acquisition of Assala Energy's assets aims to strengthen energy sovereignty and reposition the State.

image.alt: Assala Energy operator in orange coveralls, helmet and safety glasses, holding a walkie-talkie

contenu: The negotiations that led to the acquisition of Assala Energy's assets are among the most significant undertakings for Gabon's energy future. Completed in June 2024, this purchase by the Gabonese State, through Gabon Oil Company (GOC), was part of a clear strategy: to bring more of the upstream oil sector under national control, strengthen energy sovereignty and put the State back at the centre of resource governance. However, integrating the country's second-largest producer has proved complex, and recent news has been mixed, alternating between operational progress and major technical challenges.

On the one hand, Assala's production has recovered markedly. In December 2025, a 26.6% increase brought output to 57,000 barrels per day, a direct result of investment in the mature Rabi field, one of the historic pillars of Gabon's oil industry. This performance shows the ability of the State and GOC to revive mature assets, optimise existing operations and consolidate the value generated by national resources.

At the same time, however, the subsidiary has faced significant setbacks in exploration. In early 2025, three wells (Rabunga-A, Rossignol-A, Totou-NE) turned out to be dry, and another was abandoned. These failures, common in the industry but strategically sensitive for a country relaunching its oil sector, have affected Assala's ability to offset the natural decline of mature fields. They also raise questions about the exploration strategy, the quality of the geological portfolio and, above all, the transparency of management, as the figures were published late, fuelling concern among partners and industry observers.

At a time when Gabon is seeking to stabilise its oil industry to finance economic diversification, Assala plays a central role. The company must now show that it can not only sustain the performance of its mature assets but also deliver on its exploration projects. GOC, for its part, will need to turn this acquisition into a real driver of growth, innovation and energy sovereignty.

dinonga-irondu.titre: GOC becomes operator of the Dinonga and Irondou permits
dinonga-irondu.extrait: A new step in consolidating local expertise.
contenu: GOC becomes operator of the Dinonga and Irondou permits, expanding its scope for action and taking a new step in consolidating local expertise.

retrocession-addax.titre: Transfer of Addax Petroleum's assets: a historic turning point
retrocession-addax.extrait: A historic turning point in Gabon's drive to regain its energy sovereignty.

image.alt: Aerial view of the Tsiengui field facilities, deep in the forest

galerie.alt: Facilities of the Obangué field, taken over by GOC in March 2024

contenu: The takeover by Gabon Oil Company (GOC), in March 2024, of the OBANGUE and TSIENGUI fields, previously operated by Addax Petroleum, marks a decisive step in the State's recovery of its energy sovereignty.
The result of close cooperation between the Gabonese State and GOC, this asset takeover first and foremost strengthens operational management capability.
It also fully secures the share of production due to the Nation, a central issue at a time when transparency and good governance of resources have become strategic imperatives.
Finally, this transaction is a major opportunity to transfer skills to Gabonese managers and technicians.

dussafu-ezanga.titre: Ramping up: stakes in the Dussafu and Ezanga CEPPs
dussafu-ezanga.extrait: GOC gradually builds up its portfolio of strategic assets.
contenu: The company acquires stakes in the Dussafu (BW Energy) and Ezanga (Maurel & Prom Gabon) exploration and production sharing contracts (CEPP). GOC gradually builds up its portfolio of strategic assets.

perenco-participations-etat.titre: Strategic partnership with Perenco for the State's 32 interests
perenco-participations-etat.extrait: The State regains a consolidated view and stronger oversight of its asset portfolio.
contenu: GOC enters into a strategic partnership to manage the State's 32 interests in the oil assets held by Perenco Oil & Gas Gabon (POGG).
A major turning point: the State regains a consolidated view and stronger oversight of its asset portfolio.

cepp-mboga-ii.titre: Expansion on the Mboga II CEPP
cepp-mboga-ii.extrait: GOC takes over operations of the Mboga II CEPP and confirms its standing as a technical operator.
contenu: The company strengthens its activities by taking over operations of the Mboga II exploration and production sharing contract (CEPP), confirming its standing as a major technical operator.

joint-venture-bourbon.titre: First joint venture with Bourbon Gabon
joint-venture-bourbon.extrait: A key step in bringing in new expertise and strengthening national operating capacity.
contenu: GOC sets up a joint venture with Bourbon Gabon, a key step in bringing in new expertise and strengthening national operating capacity.
